name: Cebuano
variant: Cebuano of Cebu (Cebu City), everyday modern spelling
script: Latin (no extra letters), left to right
basis: Bunye and Yap, Cebuano for Beginners (University of Hawaii Press, 1971), lessons 1-30 cut down to A1: greetings and particles, kini and si / ang, ako pronouns, taga- and sa, mo- verbs, ni / sa and nako pronouns, adjectives and nga, aduna / wala, question words, mag- verbs, numbers, prices, days, time, gusto, kinahanglan, mas / labing, -on and -an verbs, maka-
src: Maria Victoria R. Bunye and Elsa Paula Yap, Cebuano for Beginners (University of Hawaii Press, 1971), table of contents of the 45 lessons (PDF via core.ac.uk)
Language Links, Magbinisaya Kita Course 1 description (grammar topics covered: non-verbal predicates, there is / has, want / like, need)
note: The order follows Bunye and Yap's contents. That book has 45 lessons from 1971; choosing which items are A1, merging them into 26 lessons, and stopping after maka- verbs is my own judgment. The family, ordering-food and directions lessons are common course practice, not lesson titles in the book. Spelling: modern everyday spelling with mo-, ug and o in final syllables (Bunye and Yap write mu-); lesson writers should keep it consistent.
hardest: Verb focus: mo- / mag- (actor) against -on / -an (goal), each with its own past form (ni- / mi-, nag-, gi-)
Three pronoun sets (ako, nako / akong, kanako) and the markers ang / si, sa / ni
Two words for 'not': dili for now and later, wala for the past and for 'there isn't'
Spanish numbers for money and time next to native Cebuano numbers

items: Sounds and spelling: three vowel sounds written five ways (i / e, u / o), ng, the glottal stop
Greetings: Maayong buntag, Kumusta ka?, Maayo man, Salamat
Small words that soften: man, lang, sab / pod, diay
kini, kana, kadto: this and that; Unsa kini?
ako-set pronouns and si / ang: Ako si…, Maestra si Ana
Introducing yourself: Taga-asa ka?, Taga-Amerika ko
Question words: unsa, kinsa, asa, ngano, kanus-a
Plural pronouns: kami and kita (we), kamo, sila
Possession: nako-set pronouns and ni / sa (balay nako, akong balay)
Adjectives and the linker nga: dakong balay, balay nga dako
There is and have: aduna, naa, wala
Numbers: usa, duha, tulo and the Spanish numbers used for money and time
Prices and buying: Tagpila?, Pila ni?, pesos
Actor-focus verbs 1: mo- (will) and ni- / mi- (did): mokaon, nikaon
Actor-focus verbs 2: mag- / nag-: magluto, nagtrabaho
dili and wala: not (now, later) and did not
Days and the clock: alas tres, Lunes, karon, ugma, gahapon
gusto, ayaw, kinahanglan: want, don't, need
Ordering food: Palihug, usa ka…, Lami!
Where things are: sa, asa, hain; diri, diha, didto
Directions and jeepneys: wala (left), tuo (right), diretso, Para!
-an verbs: doing something to or for someone (hugasan, sulatan)
Comparing: mas … kay sa, labing / pinaka-
Can and managed to: maka- / naka- (makaadto, nakakaon)
